item.title: Fiji Day public holiday on Monday 12th October
item.description: The government has declared Fiji Day public holiday on Monday 12th October 2026 instead of tomorrow. This has just been gazetted by the Fijian Government.
item.content:encoded:
The government has declared Fiji Day public holiday on Monday 12th October 2026 instead of tomorrow.

This has just been gazetted by the Fijian Government.

All the official celebrations for Fiji Day will continue tomorrow.

fijivillage News had earlier asked why a public holiday had not been allocated on a weekday to allow people to participate in celebrations and to promote patriotism, national pride and unity.

It was said that it was a norm to have the public holiday on Saturday if Fiji Day fell on that day.

item.title: Investigators check more than $300,000 in alleged suspicious transfers to former Judicial Department employee’s mobile money transfer account
item.description: Police are following the money trail after more than $50 million worth of cocaine went missing from the Suva High Court Exhibit Room, and we can confirm that investigators have established more than $300,000 in alleged suspicious transfers to a former Judicial Department employee’s mobile money transfer account. item.content:encoded:
Police are following the money trail after more than $50 million worth of cocaine went missing from the Suva High Court Exhibit Room, and we can confirm that investigators have established more than $300,000 in alleged suspicious transfers to a former Judicial Department employee’s mobile money transfer account.

Our sources confirm it is $300,000 and counting, and they are investigating the alleged suspicious transfers to the woman’s MPAiSA account.

She is currently overseas, and the investigators are trying to get her for questioning.

The woman is a close relative of an Acting Head of an independent institution in the country.

We have asked Police if they have reached out to the Acting Head to assist in locating the former Judicial Department employee. They have not made any comments on that.

When asked earlier, Police Commissioner, Rusiate Tudravu said no assumptions should be made, and everyone should allow the investigations to take its course.

The woman’s 51-year-old husband who is allegedly linked to the tampering of the drug exhibits at the Suva High Court, has been charged with one count of Interfering with Evidence and one count of Unlawful Possession of Illicit Drugs.

He has appeared in the Suva Magistrates Court.

Investigations continue with regards to the alleged involvement of others.

This case came to light after fijivillage News questioned Police on whether cocaine from the Joshua Aziz Rahman case was missing.

We had enquired about it and on 15th September, a physical check was done, after which it was confirmed by Police that 7 bars of cocaine were missing from the Rahman cocaine exhibit.

fijivillage News then received confirmation a few days later that the remaining 32 bars were tested for flour.

Those drugs were tested twice before the case, and it was confirmed to be cocaine which means they were replaced with flour.

Following this, it was also confirmed by the Police that 12 kilograms of cocaine was missing from March this year from the John Nikolic drug case.

However this information was not made public until the recent case.

Police said to us that not everything needs to be made public as it can jeopardise the investigations.

All these drug exhibits were kept at the Suva High Court Exhibit Room, and the missing cocaine is valued at more than $50 million.

Chief Justice Salesi Temo and Chief Registrar Tomasi Bainivalu are yet to respond to our questions on whether a full audit will be done at all court exhibit rooms in the country, and whether all the drug exhibits will be tested.

item.title: Rokosemudu, Sukanaisoro and Waqa remanded over alleged murder of PC Racagi, matter transferred to High Court
item.description: The three suspended Police officers who are jointly charged in relation to the alleged murder of 24-year-old Lami Police Constable Peniasi Racagi have been remanded in custody. Simione Rokosemudu, Iowane Sukanaisoro and Ilisoni Waqa appeared before Suva Magistrate Sofia Hamza.
item.content:encoded:
The three suspended Police officers who are jointly charged in relation to the alleged murder of 24-year-old Lami Police Constable Peniasi Racagi have been remanded in custody.

Simione Rokosemudu, Iowane Sukanaisoro and Ilisoni Waqa appeared before Suva Magistrate Sofia Hamza.

The matter has been transfered to the Suva High Court and will be called on the 23rd of this month. Racagi was found dead along the Lami foreshore area on the 22nd of February this year. The decision on charges against the three Police officers was made by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions after a reassessment of the investigation file and forensic results from overseas. It is alleged that the three police officers murdered Constable Racagi in February this year following an altercation.

item.title: NFP lodges police complaint over alleged threats by Paula Manumanunitoga
item.description: Nilufa Buksh , Vijay Narayan · 09/10/2026 Threatening statements about catching fellow citizens and roasting them in earth ovens must be taken seriously.
item.content:encoded:
Nilufa Buksh , Vijay Narayan · 09/10/2026

Threatening statements about catching fellow citizens and roasting them in earth ovens must be taken seriously.

This was highlighted by National Federation Party Assistant General Secretary Apenisa Vatuniveivuke, who lodged a Police complaint against Fijian Teachers Association General Secretary Paula Manumanunitoga at the CID headquarters this morning.

Vatuniveivuke says the complaint concerns what he describes as deeply disturbing, racist and threatening statements published by Manumanunitoga on Facebook.

He says the issue is not about suppressing freedom of expression, but about distinguishing between expressing an opinion and threatening fellow citizens.

Responding to questions from fijivillage News about the specific offences the party wants Police to investigate, Vatuniveivuke cited Section 17(1)(a) and (b) of the Public Order Act, Section 65(2) of the Crimes Act and Section 375 of the Crimes Act.

He says the provisions cited in the complaint relate to incitement of racial antagonism, incitement of communal antagonism, including through electronic communications, and criminal intimidation involving threats of physical injury.

Vatuniveivuke says Fiji's history of racial division and political upheaval shows the serious consequences of inflammatory statements that encourage racial hostility.

He says it is particularly disturbing that the statements allegedly came from the General Secretary of an organisation representing teachers, who are expected to promote mutual respect and help build a society free from prejudice.

Vatuniveivuke is calling on the Fiji Police Force to investigate the matter urgently and lay appropriate criminal charges if warranted.

When asked what action the party wants if an offence is established, Vatuniveivuke says they want appropriate action taken under the relevant laws.

He says the law must apply equally to everyone, regardless of their position or influence, and no Fijian should be made to feel like a stranger in their own country.

Meanwhile, NFP Leader, Professor Biman Prasad strongly condemns the racist and threatening statements published on facebook by Manumanunitoga, in which he questioned the right of fellow Fijians to belong in this country and threatened to catch people and roast them in earth ovens.

Professor Prasad describes the statements as disgraceful, dangerous and potentially criminal.

item.title: Taiwan and Fiji mark ‘Double Tenth’ with focus on cooperation and regional stability
item.description: The National Day celebration for the Republic of China (Taiwan) was held at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva last night, ahead of the Double Tenth Day celebrations. Speaking at the event, Taiwan Representative to Fiji David Cheng-Wei Wu says Taiwan has faced continued pressure and intimidation from authoritarian forces but remains determined to protect its sovereignty.
item.content:encoded:
The National Day celebration for the Republic of China (Taiwan) was held at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva last night, ahead of the Double Tenth Day celebrations.

Speaking at the event, Taiwan Representative to Fiji David Cheng-Wei Wu says Taiwan has faced continued pressure and intimidation from authoritarian forces but remains determined to protect its sovereignty.

Wu says Taiwan's investment in defence is an investment in peace, pointing to the recent return of newly acquired F-16 Block 70 fighter jets from the United States and the planned deployment of Taiwan's indigenous submarine.

He says Taiwan has the determination and capability to protect the country while continuing to support Fiji's development and contribute to the people of Fiji.

Wu also highlighted Taiwan's broader engagement in the Pacific, including its support for development, climate resilience and disaster preparedness.

Meanwhile, Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry says Taiwan is making a significant contribution to the South Pacific through its assistance in areas including climate resilience, renewable energy, agriculture, healthcare and social empowerment.

Chaudhry says Taiwan's cooperation with Fiji extends beyond government-to-government relations.

He says the relationship includes farmers learning new cultivation techniques, health professionals sharing knowledge, Fijians receiving medical assistance, young people studying in Taiwan and professionals from both countries exchanging expertise.

Chaudhry says Taiwan's assistance in agriculture could play an important role in Fiji's long-term food security.

He says Fiji can benefit from Taiwan's expertise in commercial farming, agro-industrial development, food processing, packaging, marketing and exports.

Chaudhry says Fiji has the land and climatic conditions needed to develop a range of commercial crops, while Taiwanese expertise could help strengthen the sector.

He also commended Taiwan's economic development, saying Fiji has much to learn from its progress as a small island economy.

Chaudhry says Taiwan's development has been driven by democratic and economic freedoms, good governance, hard work and determination.

He says the two island nations share similar challenges associated with their size and economies, while Taiwan has managed to overcome many of those constraints.
